title: Building your home gym: budget & space management
summary: Practical guide to planning a home gym: build it all at once or piece by piece, budget by retailer to use free-shipping thresholds, watch out for split shipments and delivery logistics, and above all map the space in advance (chalk outline, numbered equipment list, rack first with clearance). He built his 16x8 ft garage gym in one month. The description warns not to build one mid-pandemic.

claims.claim: Don't build a home gym in the middle of a crisis; do calisthenics at home and build it once things blow over.
Building a home gym bit by bit is viable and spreads cost and effort; buying everything at once saves money on shipping and gives peace of mind.
Being extremely meticulous, he built his whole home gym at once, about one month from start of preparation to fully assembled, and is glad he did now that gyms are closed.
Account for every cost; know where you can go cheap, but pay for quality on key items: a good barbell lasts 10 years, a bad one may be done in two.
Check stock before ordering bundles: retailers may hold the whole shipment for one out-of-stock item; call and ask them to ship that piece later, usually at no extra cost.
Use order thresholds for discounts and free shipping (e.g. Rogue over 5000 USD, many plate sellers over 500 USD), but don't buy a piece you like less just to hit a threshold.
Plan delivery dates: be present to receive big items, and make sure carriers bring heavy items inside rather than leaving 500 lbs of plates on the curb.
Space planning is the key part: draw a map of the space so you don't discover on build day that equipment doesn't fit.
If you build a platform, it comes first and the gym goes on top of it.
His whole gym fits in a 16 by 8 ft space in a garage full of mechanical equipment.
Measure the space and chalk its exact outline on the floor, then sit and visualise where every piece will go, since bolted pieces can't move later.
List every piece of equipment with a number (e.g. 1-10) and place the numbers on the paper plan, keeping each item's real footprint in mind; construction video games train this skill.
The rack is the centrepiece and should come first; avoid putting it in the middle, which wastes space in front and behind. His sits near the back.
A home gym is a 3D project: leave clearance on both sides of the rack for loading plates and for your body, and padding if you pull from the floor.
Plan months in advance and don't over-pack; a cramped, non-ergonomic gym kills enthusiasm to train.
